title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a fragment of a systematic list of formal properties of Euler characteristics of topological spaces. Earlier items (a)–(e) are presumably on preceding manuscript pages; the neighbouring images are unrelated administrative typescripts used as scrap paper.

Setting: k is a field.
- E_{χ!} is the class of spaces X whose compactly supported cohomology H^*_!(X,k) has finite total dimension. For these, χ_!(X) = Σ(-1)^p dim H^p_!(X,k).
- E_χ is the analogous class for ordinary (co)homology, with χ(X) = Σ(-1)^p dim H^p(X,k).

(f) Multiplicativity under products. If X,Y ∈ E_{χ!} then X×Y ∈ E_{χ!} and χ_!(X×Y) = χ_!(X)χ_!(Y). This is Künneth for compact supports. The same holds for E_χ and χ, using Künneth for homology H_*(X×Y,k) and then dualising (H^* = (H_*)^∨ over a field). The parenthesis remarks that this suggests an interpretation of the class E_χ and of the value of χ, presumably through homology rather than cohomology.

(g) Multiplicativity in locally trivial fibrations. Let f: X → Y be locally trivial with fibre F, and Y,F ∈ E_{χ!}. Then X ∈ E_{χ!} and χ_!(X) = χ_!(Y)χ_!(F). The ordinary χ version is stated as analogous.

Proof of (g) via the Leray spectral sequence with proper supports:
- E_2^{p,q} = H^p_!(Y, R^q f_! k_X) ⇒ H^{p+q}_!(X).
- Each R^q f_! k_X is a local system on Y with fibre H^q_!(F).
- If E_2 is finite-dimensional, so is the abutment, and χ_!(X) = Σ_q (-1)^q χ_!(Y, R^q f_! k).
- This reduces to a Lemma: for a local system R of rank b on Y ∈ E_{χ!}, χ_!(Y,R) is defined and equals b·χ_!(Y). Then χ_!(X) = χ_!(Y) Σ(-1)^q b^q_!(F) = χ_!(Y)χ_!(F).

Proof of the Lemma, in the cellular case. Suppose Y has a finite filtration by closed subspaces with Y_i − Y_{i−1} a finite disjoint union of cells Z_ij ≅ R^{d_ij}. Then:
- additivity of χ_! over open/closed decompositions (long exact sequence of compactly supported cohomology) gives χ_!(Y,R) = Σ χ_!(Z_ij, R);
- R is trivial on each contractible cell, so χ_!(Z_ij,R) = b·χ_!(Z_ij) = b(−1)^{d_ij};
- summing back gives b·χ_!(Y).

In modern terms, this is the standard toolkit showing that χ_c is additive and multiplicative: it defines a ring homomorphism from a Grothendieck ring of (cellular / constructible) spaces to Z, and it is insensitive to monodromy of local systems. This is the topological prototype of the Euler–Poincaré formulas of SGA 5 and of Euler-characteristic integration.
errors: In the Demonstration, Grothendieck writes 'X ∈ E_χ et χ(X) = …' but the computation uses H_! throughout. The class and invariant should be E_{χ!} and χ_!(X).
In the Lemma, χ_!(Y,R) is defined as Σ(-1)^p H^p(Y,R). It should be Σ(-1)^p dim H^p_!(Y,R): compact supports, and ranks rather than the vector spaces themselves.

Gap acknowledged on the page: the Lemma is proved only when Y admits a finite cell stratification. For an arbitrary Y ∈ E_{χ!} (finite total compactly supported Betti numbers only), finiteness of H^*_!(Y,R) for non-trivial local systems is not automatic. The proof sketch therefore does not cover the full class E_{χ!}.

The 'énoncé analogue' for ordinary χ needs the corresponding lemma for H^*(Y,R) with R^q f_* (and a finiteness hypothesis). For spaces of infinite type with finite total Betti numbers, non-trivial local systems can have infinite-dimensional cohomology, so extra hypotheses (e.g. finite CW) are needed.
Implicit: Y and F must be reasonable spaces (locally compact, etc.) for proper base change, so that R^q f_! k is the local system with fibre H^q_!(F).

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard textbook properties of the (compactly supported) Euler characteristic, written out as course- or seminar-style notes. The only flavour is the brief hint at 'interpreting' E_χ and χ via homology duality, but it is undeveloped.
transcription_corrections: 'd'où qui permet de tenter l'interprétation' is likely 'ce qui permet de tenter l'interprétation de E_χ et la valeur de χ …'.
'sous réserve finissant que E_2^{**} de dim finie' is likely 'sous réserve de finitude, que E_2^{**} de dim finie' (i.e. 'provided E_2 is finite-dimensional').
'(car triv. Z_ij)' under the sum likely reads '(car R triv. sur Z_ij)'.
In the Lemma the insertion above 'rang' is 'fini' (rank finite b), and 'sur [crossed out] Y ∈ E_{χ!}' is a deletion of something like 'X loc. compact'.
In 'Marche droit au moins si gr_? Y admet filtration finie', the inserted symbol may be a marginal annotation rather than 'gr'; 'triangulable' is struck out.
The marginal note left of (g) is illegible; 'avec ligne générale du sel' is doubtful.
